cause: a value under a key made of an item's text held ids that are of the item's file
whys: why wrong: two impls with one key made two values
why possible: the value encoded `ErasedFileAstId`s, which depend on the file's other items, and the key is position-free by design (rule 65: an edit elsewhere in the file must not move it)
why written so: the module said `the values name nothing of a database`, which is true, and an ast id was taken to be of the item; nothing said a value must also name nothing of a file

why not caught by the tests: the fixture's impls were `S0`..`S3`, each with its own text, so no two items shared a key; the oracle compared `kind name` text `no database's ids are in`, dropping the one thing that was wrong; and the test store serves a put back at once, so even twins would have been a silent wrong read where the driver (a get does not see the build's own puts) refuses
why not caught before green: green was said from unit tests and a check; the smoke, which docs/harness.md already says a gate run cannot skip, had not been run on that head
property: an entry keyed by content held a position
class: content-keyed value with a position-relative encoding (rule 25's kin: an id where a name belongs); the same class as a crate id, an interned id or an address in a store value, and as the select bug of the same day (a pointer key without its file), seen from the other side
prevention: The encoding cannot say it any more: an `assoc items` value (layout 2) names an item by its place among those written in its impl, and the reader takes the ast id from its own file's index (`FileIndex::assoc_items`, file index layout 2), so a value read by any impl can name only that impl's own items, and decode refuses a place or a kind the reader's impl does not have. Tests in `entries/items/tests.rs`: twins read their own items (oracle with ast ids); twins make one value within one build (`Memory::within_one_build`, the driver's get/put behaviour); the control `the_oracle_catches_an_ast_id_in_an_assoc_value` plants layout 1's value (`IDS_IN_VALUE`) and gets both the wrong read and the refusal; `an_entry_is_the_same_bytes_wherever_its_item_is_written` checks equal keys are equal bytes across two files for every family asked. The refusal names the item (first line, file:line, which build of the crate, ast id) and how the values differ (`entries::differ`: lengths, first differing byte, bytes there), in `Memory` and in the driver's `Images::ask`. Open: no type stops the next family from encoding an `ErasedFileAstId` under a text key (a writer type for such values that has no method taking an ast id would); the cfg part of both keys is the crate's whole cfg where the text names `cfg`, not the atoms read; the gate must not call a head green before the smoke ran on it.
